advances: The actual polygonal signed roof and first-order sufficient descent under explicit endpoint gap or tie conditions.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The midpoint set $(A_\varepsilon+B)/2$ is the convex hull of $(A+B)/2$ and $(p+\varepsilon n+B)/2$. The first set has exposed face exactly $I_0$ in direction $n$, so its vertices there satisfy the roof inequality since $G\ge0$ on $I_0$, and its other vertices have fixed strictly negative $t$. The vertices of the second seed from $F_B$ lie on $J$ at height $\varepsilon/2$ and obey the roof, while every other vertex has strictly negative limiting $t$. All unchanged $K$ facet inequalities hold on the second seed by the strict slack at the old apex $p$ from the shared-face enlargement proof. Hence convexity gives the full midpoint inclusion for small $\varepsilon$. The unchanged inequalities together with $t\le\varepsilon/2$ give uniform boundedness. Every fixed compact subset of $\operatorname{int}K$ lies inside the new polygon for small $\varepsilon$, and every limit point of the new polygons lies in $K$. Thus they converge in Hausdorff distance and contain a fixed disk around $y_0$. The three-site hull realizes exactly the new polygons by the midpoint inclusion.

The symmetric difference from $K$ lies in a band $|t|\le C\varepsilon$ for some constant $C$, because $G$ is bounded on the common bounded domain. Inside this band the two adjacent nonparallel facets constrain the tangential coordinate to $[a-O(\varepsilon),b+O(\varepsilon)]$. Away from tangential intervals of length $O(\varepsilon)$ around $a,b$, all other facet bounds permit the full signed strip between $t=0$ and $t=\varepsilon G(s)/2$: their slacks along $F_K$ are affine and bounded below by a positive constant times the distance to the endpoints, unless bounded below on the whole face. Thus the corner area error is $O(\varepsilon^2)$. A proper cap parallel to the face is separated from the strip. For each transverse proper cap the possible mismatch between its strip signature and its original face signature, even with $O(\varepsilon)$ level motion, is in another tangential interval of length $O(\varepsilon)$ and has area $O(\varepsilon^2)$. The same bounds hold for the added $A$ triangle. The scalar inverse-level argument in the shared-face enlargement proof therefore gives a whole-middle-plane menu with raw budget $q_\varepsilon^s=Q+\varepsilon q_s'+o(\varepsilon)$, where
$$
q_s'=\int_{F_A}T_p W_A\,ds+\tfrac12\int_{F_K}G W_K\,ds.
$$
The actual mass derivative is $D_s=L_A/2+\tfrac12\int_{F_K}G\,ds$, so $C_s=q_s'-rD_s$. On $I_0$ the profile is the unit-height trapezoid with base length $(L_A+L_B)/2$ and top length $L_B/2$. The positive middle contribution is $L_A/8+L_B/4$. The two negative linear extensions have respective slopes $2/d_L,-2/d_R$ before multiplication by $1/2$. Integration gives their costs $-\ell_L^2/(2d_L)$ and $-\ell_R^2/(2d_R)$. Cauchy–Schwarz and $d_L+d_R=L_A$ yield the stated supremum. With two positive excesses equality occurs at the proportional distances; with one positive excess the supremum is approached at the appropriate boundary, and with both zero it is attained at every interior apex.

By 2acc8bc803acf1c0 each endpoint depth is ordinary, and the enlarged $A$ retains its strict gap by the uniform area bound on each cap, including for points new to $A$. The $B$ depth is unchanged. With two strict gaps the middle menu controls the new raw maximum for small $\varepsilon$, giving coefficient $C_s/M$. With a tied $B$ the upper bound is $\max(Q,q_\varepsilon^s)$ before dividing by the actual mass $M+\varepsilon D_s+o(\varepsilon)$. Its normalized first-order numerator is $\max(q_s',0)-rD_s=\max(C_s,-rD_s)$, which is negative exactly under the two asserted inequalities because $r>0$. Both are evaluated at the same apex.
statement:
Keep the data and enlarged $A_\varepsilon$ of pk-w33-coupled-shared-polygon-face-enlargement. In a unit tangential coordinate write $F_K=[a,b]$, $I_0=(F_A+F_B)/2=[a_0,b_0]$ and $J=[c,d]$, so $a\le a_0<c\le d<b_0\le b$. With $t=n\cdot x-h_K(n)$, retain the other $K$ facet inequalities and replace $t\le0$ by $t\le(\varepsilon/2)G(s)$, where
$$
G(s)=\min\{1,(s-a_0)/(c-a_0),(b_0-s)/(b_0-d)\}.
$$
This defines an actual compatible polygonal path $A_\varepsilon,K_\varepsilon^s,B$. Put $\ell_L=a_0-a,\ \ell_R=b-b_0$, and let $d_L,d_R$ be the apex distances to the left and right endpoints of $F_A$, respectively. Its total mixed mass has right derivative
$$
D_s=\tfrac{5L_A}{8}+\tfrac{L_B}{4}-\tfrac{\ell_L^2}{2d_L}-\tfrac{\ell_R^2}{2d_R}.
$$
The moving equal-budget menu has normalized first-response numerator $C_s=C_A+\tfrac12\int_{F_K}G(W_K-r)\,ds$, where $C_A=\int_{F_A}T_p(W_A-r)\,ds$. The supremum of $D_s$ over interior apices is $5L_A/8+L_B/4-(\ell_L+\ell_R)^2/(2L_A)$.

If $Q$ is the original global raw maximum and both ordinary endpoint maxima are strictly below $Q$, then $C_s<0$ gives strict descent. If the $A$ gap is strict and the unchanged $B$ maximum equals $Q$, strict negativity of the first-order normalized upper certificate is equivalent to $D_s>0$ and $C_s<0$.
title: A compatible signed roof and its exact tied-endpoint test
